items.q: Do we really have to wait a year before using the water?
items.a: No. WHO TRS 1033 allows use from phase 2 when data show the required quality and your quality unit approves. The year covers seasonal feed water changes.

items.q: Can IQ and OQ be combined into one protocol?
items.a: Yes, depending on complexity, under EU good manufacturing practice (GMP) Annex 15, 2.5 and 3.10. On a single module it saves a review cycle; on the full package we keep them apart.

items.q: What counts as passing IQ and OQ?
items.a: The criteria written in each protocol, which your validation team approves before testing starts. The summary lists every test as met or not met. Each miss carries its deviation number, action and owner. Your quality unit decides release.

items.q: We work to ASTM E2500, not IQ/OQ/PQ. Can you?
items.a: Yes. Under ASTM E2500 the tests are much the same, focused on the critical aspects your risk assessment names.

items.q: What if an action level is exceeded during PQ?
items.a: It is a deviation under your procedure. We help find the root cause (WHO TRS 1033, 12.9); resampling verifies the fix. The phase may be extended.

items.q: Can you qualify a system you did not build?
items.a: For [makes and equipment types serviced]: we start with a system assessment of its qualification file and the installed system.

items.q: Natural health products: do we need IQ, OQ and PQ?
items.a: GUI-0158's water sections (45 and 46) do not name IQ, OQ and PQ. They ask for criteria to qualify and monitor treated water, test records, and calibrated, maintained equipment. Our scope for that evidence: [NHP qualification scope]. Where your quality assurance person (QAP) asks for IQ, OQ and PQ, the path on this page applies.

items.q: Do you train the people who will run it?
items.a: Yes, on your system after start-up: [training hours and audiences]. Training ends when your operators can run the system and clear its usual alarms. Each trainee signs a record, tied to the manual chapter covered, for your quality file.
